title: Conduction and Thermal Conductivity
notes: **Conduction:** heat transfer through a material without bulk motion of the material. Energy is passed from molecule to molecule via collisions and vibrations.
**Thermal conductivity $k$:** the amount of heat flowing per unit time through unit area per unit temperature gradient. $H = -kA\frac{dT}{dx}$.

**Fourier's law:** the negative sign indicates heat flows from hot to cold. $k$ depends on material: metals have high $k$ because free electrons carry energy; gases have low $k$ because molecules are far apart.
**Measurement:** Searle's apparatus or Forbes's method compares heat flow through a rod to the heat gained by water, giving $k$ from measured temperature changes and dimensions.
**Why metals feel cold:** metals conduct heat away from your hand faster than insulators, making them feel colder even at the same temperature.
